project.name: DriftHR
project.description: HRMS & Payroll (India + NZ) — multi-tenant, white-label SaaS. Tenant HR console (app-staging), white-label Employee Self-Service (demo-staging), and Super Admin (admin-staging). Core invariants tested throughout: tenant isolation, hierarchical RBAC (a manager only sees/acts on their own reporting sub-tree), and maker-checker separation of duties on money.
project.note: Login endpoints have an aggressive rate limiter (HTTP 429) — space out automated logins.

logins.label: HR Admin (maker)
logins.scopeNote: Full tenant access (ALL scope band). Runs HR org-wide and is the 'maker' in maker-checker: can run/submit a payroll run but cannot approve it for disbursement. Configures org, roles, branding, letters, recruitment, onboarding.

logins.label: Finance (checker)
logins.scopeNote: Money, not people (ALL financial scope). The 'checker' in maker-checker: approves payroll runs and compensation revisions, views comp tenant-wide, files returns. Cannot create/terminate employees or approve leave.

logins.label: Manager (Aarav)
logins.scopeNote: TEAM band — sees and acts on ONLY his own reporting sub-tree (direct + indirect reports via the reporting tree). Can approve his team's leave and manage their attendance. Has NO compensation/payroll access. The security-critical role: out-of-team records return 404, never another team's data.

logins.label: Employee (Priya)
logins.scopeNote: Self-service only (SELF band), on the white-label Employee portal. Sees only her own profile, payslips, leave, attendance, letters. Subject is always derived from her session — she can never read another employee's data.

logins.label: Employee (Meera)
logins.scopeNote: Second self-service employee, used for cross-employee isolation tests (e.g. confirming one employee cannot see another's payslip/profile). SELF band on the Employee portal.

logins.label: Super Admin
logins.scopeNote: Platform operator on the Super Admin host. Provisions/runs tenants and the SaaS business; bypasses tenant gates but every privileged read/impersonation is audited. Never used for day-to-day HR.

features.title: Login, Roles & Hierarchical Scopes
features.summary: The authorization spine of DriftHR: who can do what (action permissions) AND over whom (data scope from the reporting tree). It is what makes 'a manager manages only their own employees' true by construction.
features.howItWorks:
Authorization is a pair: (action, scope). Holding a permission is necessary but not sufficient — every action also resolves a DATA SCOPE from the reporting tree, and the two are ANDed on every query.

- Five system roles: Owner & HR-Admin (ALL band), Manager (TEAM band = own reporting sub-tree), Finance (ALL financial), Employee (hard SELF).
- A Manager has NO `canViewCompensation` by default — salary never serializes into a manager-scoped payload.
- Out-of-scope single-row access returns 404 (never reveals existence); lists are filtered, never 403'd.
- Roles & per-user assignment are managed in Settings > Roles; the org/reporting tree is set via the org chart. Editing a role takes effect on the user's next request (no re-login).
features.notes: Live. RBAC is Feature 1 (done) and underpins every other module's scoping.

Open People.
Note the count and the names listed.
useCases.expected: The People list shows ONLY Aarav's reporting sub-tree (his direct and indirect reports), not the whole company. Total equals the sub-tree size; peers/other teams are absent.

useCases.title: Manager cannot open a non-report's record (IDOR-safe 404)
steps: Log in as aarav.sharma@demo.test.
Open People and copy the URL of one of your own reports (it ends in /people/<id>).
Edit the URL to point at an employee who is NOT in your team (e.g. swap in another employee id) and load it.

useCases.title: HR Admin assigns a role and it takes effect immediately
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test.
Open Settings > Roles.
Review the 5 system roles and the per-user role assignment table; note system roles are read-only/duplicatable.
(Optional) reassign a non-critical user's role and confirm the change saves.
useCases.expected: The roles matrix (15 permission keys) and the people-to-role table load. Changes save without error; you cannot strip the last Owner (guarded with a 409-style message).

features.title: Onboarding & Employee Lifecycle
features.summary: Turns an accepted offer into a fully provisioned, active employee through a tracked onboarding pipeline, and runs the reverse (separation -> Full & Final settlement) at exit.
features.howItWorks:
Hire -> onboard -> active as a pipeline:
- An accepted offer seeds an onboarding journey with a checklist; the new hire self-onboards (personal/statutory/bank + document upload + e-sign) before day one.
- HR clicks 'Provision' once -> atomically creates the Employee + portal User + role + manager link + compensation + leave (all-or-nothing; re-click is a no-op).
- Probation -> confirm -> Active.
- Separation: initiate -> exit clearance checklist -> compute FnF (gratuity IN / holiday payout NZ / leave encashment / notice / asset & loan recovery) -> approve (separate approver) -> pay via an FnF pay run -> relieving/experience letters.
Managers see only their own reports' lifecycle tasks (TEAM band); a new/exiting employee sees only themselves.
features.notes: Live. Provisioning is atomic and idempotent; FnF approval is separation-of-duties gated (initiator cannot approve).

useCases.title: View the onboarding pipeline board
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test.
Open Onboarding.
Review the pipeline columns (Offer Sent -> Accepted -> Onboarding -> Active) and any cards with their task-progress ring and blocking-task badge.
useCases.expected: The pipeline board renders columns and cards. A card cannot reach 'Active' while a blocking task is open or a required e-sign document is unsigned.

useCases.title: Initiate a separation and review the FnF runner
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test.
Open Separations.
Open (or initiate) a separation case and review the three panes: clearance checklist, FnF preview, and the status timeline.
useCases.expected: The separation runner shows clearance lanes, an FnF preview (gratuity / leave encashment / notice / recoveries), and a status timeline. Settle is gated on all clearance lanes cleared + FnF approved + zero un-returned assets.

useCases.title: Initiator cannot approve their own FnF (separation of duties)
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test (the person who initiated/computed the separation).
Open the separation case and compute FnF.
Attempt to approve the FnF as the same user.
useCases.expected: Approve is disabled/blocked for the initiator — FnF approval requires a different actor (a Finance/checker holding payroll-approval). The system never lets the maker approve their own settlement.

useCases.title: Admin clears exit assets during separation
steps: Open a separation case for a leaving employee.
In the Exit assets section, for each outstanding asset click Mark returned, or Record recovery to log a non-recovered amount.
useCases.expected: Each open asset is resolved; the asset-return lane clears and the exit can proceed to FnF compute/settle (which was previously blocked with no UI path).

features.title: Attendance & Time
features.summary: Captures punches, derives a deterministic daily attendance status (present/absent/half-day/leave/holiday/LOP), and freezes the payable result into payroll. Regularization fixes go through manager approval.
features.howItWorks:
Punch -> daily rollup -> freeze to payroll:
- An employee clocks in/out (ESS); a pure derivation engine turns punches + schedule + leave + holidays into exactly one Attendance row per (employee, day) with status and LOP fraction.
- A leave day is ON_LEAVE, never ABSENT; holidays/weekly-offs are recognised.
- HR runs a period close that locks the period and freezes payable days/LOP/overtime into the payroll feed (immutable once frozen).
- Regularization (missed punch / WFH / on-duty): the employee self-raises -> routes to their manager -> on approve, punches are materialized and the day re-derived.
Manager sees only their sub-tree's board and decisions; out-of-scope target -> 404.
features.notes: Live. Derivation engine is golden-tested; freeze is monotonic and immutable. Multi-mode capture (geo + IP + face selfie) policy is configurable in Settings > Attendance > Capture.

useCases.title: Daily punch (happy path)
steps: Log in as priya.nair@demo.test on the Employee portal.
Open Attendance.
Click Punch In, wait a moment, then click Punch Out.
useCases.expected: Today's row shows an in-time, out-time, total hours, and status = Present.

useCases.title: Employee raises a regularization, manager approves it
steps: As priya.nair@demo.test (Employee portal), open Attendance and raise a correction/regularization (e.g. a missed punch) with a date, requested in/out and reason.
Log in as aarav.sharma@demo.test on the HR Admin portal and open Attendance.
Find the pending regularization in the team queue and Approve it.
useCases.expected: Priya's request appears only in her manager's queue (not elsewhere). On approval the corrected punches materialize and the day is re-derived to the corrected status.

useCases.title: HR runs a period close (lock + freeze)
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test on the HR Admin portal.
Open Attendance and go to the Period Close / dashboard area.
Reconcile any blockers, then lock the period.
useCases.expected: The period locks; further punches/regularizations in that range are blocked, and the payable result (payable days, LOP, overtime) is frozen for payroll. Locked rows do not retro-mutate.

features.title: Leave Management
features.summary: End-to-end leave: accrual of entitlements, an apply -> approve flow with policy checks, balances and calendar, year-end carry-forward/lapse, and encashment at exit. India + NZ (Holidays Act) aware.
features.howItWorks:
Entitlement lifecycle + request flow over an append-only ledger:
- Balances accrue (monthly/upfront/anniversary/NZ-continuous) via a nightly job; carry-forward and lapse run at year-end.
- Apply: the engine computes working-day-aware days (skips leading/trailing weekoffs & holidays), runs policy gates (notice, max-consecutive, balance, tenure, gender), and places a soft-hold on the balance.
- Approve: routes to the applicant's manager (escalates up the chain, HR fallback). The manager is excluded from approving their own leave (SoD). On approve the hold becomes 'taken'.
- A paid leave day shows as ON_LEAVE in attendance, not absent; LWP (unpaid) drives LOP into payroll.
Closing = opening + accrued - taken - encashed - lapsed + adjusted (the ledger invariant).
features.notes: Live. Available balance = closing - pendingApproval (the ESS card shows this, not raw closing).

useCases.title: Employee applies for leave; available drops by the held amount
steps: Log in as priya.nair@demo.test on the Employee portal.
Open Leave > Apply.
Pick a leave type, a start and end date (optionally a half-day), add a reason if required, and Submit.
Check the My Balances tab.
useCases.expected: A PENDING request is created with the correct computed day count (weekends/holidays inside the range not charged). 'Available' immediately drops by the held amount; the request shows in My Requests as Pending.

useCases.title: Manager approves a direct report's leave
steps: Ensure Priya (a report of Aarav) has a pending leave request.
Log in as aarav.sharma@demo.test on the HR Admin portal and open Leave > Requests.
Open the request and Approve it.
useCases.expected: The request appears only in Aarav's queue. On approve, the status becomes Approved and Priya's balance moves from held to taken atomically.

useCases.title: A user cannot approve their own leave (SoD)
steps: Log in as aarav.sharma@demo.test on the HR Admin portal.
Apply for leave for himself (via ESS or as a self-request).
Open Leave > Requests and look for his own request to approve.
useCases.expected: Aarav cannot approve his own leave — the approve action is absent for his own request and it routes up to his manager/HR instead.

useCases.title: Admin withdraws an already-approved leave
steps: Open Leave > Requests as the HR admin.
Find a request whose status is APPROVED or AVAILED.
Click Withdraw and confirm.
useCases.expected: The leave is withdrawn (status WITHDRAWN), the balance is credited back, and any comp-off is re-credited. If the pay run for that month is closed, a clear 'closed pay run' message appears and nothing changes.

features.title: Compensation & CTC
features.summary: Salary structures and CTC: build a structure with a live CTC -> gross -> net preview, assign/revise an employee's pay with maker-checker approval, and enforce the India 'Basic >= 50% CTC' wage rule. Salary is masked by role.
features.howItWorks:
Structure builder + revisions, all reconciling to the payroll engine to the paise:
- HR builds a salary structure (components + a BALANCING special allowance) and sees a live waterfall: CTC -> minus employer cost -> gross -> minus deductions -> net, with the India 50% guard chip.
- Assigning/revising pay is append-only and effective-dated; a revision can be proposed by a maker and must be approved by a different checker (self-approve is blocked).
- The India 50% rule (Basic+DA >= 50% of CTC) is enforced fail-closed at preview and at save; it is skipped for NZ.
- Field-level masking on every read: a manager without the comp grant gets a RANGE envelope (band/compa-ratio), never an absolute figure; the number is omitted server-side, not blurred. Employees see only their own.
features.notes: Live for the per-employee revision maker-checker flow. The bulk increment-cycle worksheet is deliberately deferred to a later phase (the Approvals tab signposts this; no dead increment-cycle tab is shown).

useCases.title: Build a salary structure and watch the live CTC->net preview
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test.
Open Compensation > Structures.
Add/edit a structure: set the header (name, country, currency, basis), add component lines including one BALANCING special allowance, and set a target CTC.
Watch the right-hand live preview.
useCases.expected: The waterfall (CTC -> employer cost -> gross -> deductions -> net) updates live and the India 50% guard chip is green when Basic+DA >= 50% of CTC.

useCases.title: India wage-floor blocks a structure with Basic below 50%
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test and open Compensation > Structures (an India entity).
Build a structure where Basic+DA is set below 50% of CTC.
Attempt to Save.
useCases.expected: The 50% guard chip turns red and Save is blocked (client + server) with a clear message — the structure cannot be saved until Basic+DA >= 50% of CTC.

useCases.title: Maker cannot approve their own compensation revision (SoD)
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test, open Compensation > Revisions, pick an employee and propose a revision (new CTC or % hike); save as Proposed.
Still as operator@demo.test, try to approve that same revision.
Then log in as finance@demo.test and approve it.
useCases.expected: Self-approval is rejected (SOD_SELF_APPROVAL). The revision can only be approved by a different checker (Finance), after which it becomes Effective.

useCases.title: Employee views only their own CTC breakup
steps: Log in as priya.nair@demo.test on the Employee portal.
Open Compensation.
Review the CTC breakup waterfall, revision history, and any increment letters.
useCases.expected: Priya sees her own full CTC breakup (earnings, employee deductions, and employer contributions labelled 'cost to company'). There is no way to view anyone else's pay — the page is always self-scoped.

features.title: Payroll Run (Maker-Checker)
features.summary: The guided pay-run workflow: compute payslips, review period-over-period variance, then maker submits and a separate finance checker approves before disbursement, payslip publish, and statutory filing.
features.howItWorks:
Lifecycle: Draft -> Inputs locked -> Computed -> In review -> Approved -> Paid -> Filed -> Closed.
- Maker (operator, canRunPayroll): creates a run with entity/calendar pickers, freezes attendance, computes payslips, reviews the PRE-RUN CHECKS panel (period-over-period deltas + cross-employee + absolute sanity rules, grouped BLOCKER/WARNING/INFO with per-employee drill-down and a plain-language summary), then Submits for approval.
- Checker (finance, canApprovePayroll): reviews and Approves — or Sends back with a reason.
- HARD RULES enforced server-side and mirrored in the UI: no state-skipping; maker != checker (approve 409s if the actor computed the run); blocking anomalies gate approval; approved/paid/filed runs are immutable; recompute with unchanged inputs is a cached no-op.
- After approval: Mark Paid -> payslips publish to ESS -> country-aware filing exports (IN ECR/ESIC/24Q; NZ payday EI + bank batch) -> File -> Close.
- PRE-RUN ANOMALY REVIEW: a dedicated Checks tab groups every finding by severity with the suggested fix and per-employee drill-down. New cross-employee checks include DUPLICATE BANK ACCOUNT (two payees sharing one account = blocker) and statutory wage-base discontinuity. The tolerances the checks use are tunable per tenant (Variance tolerances editor, canRunPayroll).
- ACKNOWLEDGE / OVERRIDE GATE: blocking anomalies gate approval, but a checker (canApprovePayroll) can explicitly ACKNOWLEDGE a blocker WITH A REASON (audited) to clear the gate for that finding. Approval proceeds only when every blocker is resolved or acknowledged; a maker cannot waive their own blockers (acknowledge is a checker action).
features.notes: Live. Compute engine, state machine, and filing generators are golden-tested. The headline test surface is the maker-checker SoD: operator submits, finance approves. Pre-run checks are a pure, golden-tested engine; the acknowledge/override is audited and gated on canApprovePayroll.

useCases.title: Maker creates, computes and submits a pay run
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test.
Open Payroll and click New Run; pick an Entity and its Pay calendar (the period auto-fills) — no raw UUIDs.
Work the inputs checklist (freeze attendance), then Compute.
Open the Variance tab and review deltas, then click Submit for approval.
useCases.expected: The run advances Draft -> Computed -> In review. Submit is disabled while any BLOCKER anomaly is open. After submit the maker's view is read-only and the run is queued for a checker.

useCases.title: Finance checker approves the submitted run
steps: Log in as finance@demo.test.
Open Payroll and find the run that is In review.
Review the read-only variance, then click Approve (or Send back with a reason).
useCases.expected: Finance can Approve the run (maker != checker, zero blockers). On approve it moves to Approved; the audit records the preparer and the four-eyes reviewer.

useCases.title: Maker reviews the pre-run checks panel
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test.
Open a computed pay run and click the Checks tab.
Read the Payroll health summary (N blockers, M warnings, net-pay swing) and the plain-language paragraph.
Expand the severity groups (Blockers / Warnings / Context) and use Drill on a flagged employee to see the line detail and suggested action.
Optionally open Variance tolerances and adjust a threshold (e.g. net swing warn-at), Save, then re-open Checks to see the effect.
useCases.expected: The Checks tab shows a readable, grouped review of every finding with the suggested fix and per-employee drill-down, paginated for large runs. A one-line summary and a deterministic plain-language paragraph describe the run. Editing a tolerance (canRunPayroll) changes which findings are raised.

useCases.title: Checker acknowledges a blocker with a reason, then approves
steps: Log in as finance@demo.test and open a run (Computed or In review) that has at least one blocking anomaly.
Go to the Approval (or Checks) tab; note the Approve button is disabled while an unacknowledged blocker is open.
Click Acknowledge on a blocker, enter a reason in the override modal, and confirm.
Once every blocker shows Acknowledged, click Approve.
useCases.expected: Approve is gated while any blocker is unacknowledged. After the checker acknowledges each blocker with a reason (recorded against their name), the gate clears and Approve succeeds. The acknowledgement ledger lists who overrode what and why.

useCases.title: Approval stays blocked until every blocker is resolved or acknowledged
steps: Log in as finance@demo.test and open a run that has two or more blocking anomalies.
Acknowledge only ONE of the blockers (with a reason).
Attempt to Approve.
useCases.expected: Approve remains blocked (button disabled and a server OPEN_BLOCKERS 409 on any direct attempt) while even one blocker is still unacknowledged. Only after every blocker is acknowledged-with-reason or resolved does approval proceed — the gate is operable, never a silent bypass.

useCases.title: Maker cannot approve their own run (maker-checker)
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test (the user who computed and submitted the run).
Open the same run that is In review.
Look for and attempt the Approve action.
useCases.expected: The Approve button is hidden for the maker with a banner ('You computed this run — approval requires a different reviewer'); any direct attempt returns a MAKER_CHECKER 409. The maker can never approve their own run by any path.

useCases.title: Employee sees a payslip only after it is published
steps: Log in as priya.nair@demo.test on the Employee portal.
Open Payslips.
Confirm a payslip appears only for a run that has been Paid/published; open it and download the PDF.
useCases.expected: Only published (Paid) payslips are listed. The download is the employee's own payslip PDF — never the run-level bank/statutory file. First open flips the payslip to Viewed.

features.title: Performance & Goals
features.summary: Goals/OKRs and a review cycle (self -> manager -> calibrate -> release -> acknowledge), with basic calibration and an optional merit recommendation handed to compensation. Scoped to the reporting tree with reviewer != reviewee SoD.
features.howItWorks:
Review cycle + goals over the reporting tree:
- HR configures a cycle (template + rating scale), launches it (bulk-mints one review per employee, auto-assigning the manager as reviewer), and tracks completion.
- Flow: employee submits self-review -> manager submits manager-review (reviewer must differ from reviewee) -> HR/skip-level calibrate -> HR releases -> employee acknowledges.
- Ratings stay hidden from the employee until release (release gate); a manager only sees/acts on their own sub-tree's reviews (out-of-scope -> 404).
- Goals/OKRs: weighted progress rolls up from key-result check-ins; a manager cannot rate themselves.
- On close, an eligible review emits a merit recommendation; compensation (a separate approval) decides and applies it.
features.notes: Partially live: the console ships review-operations surfaces (My Team Reviews + cycle list/launch/release/stats) first. Goals/OKR authoring, calibration-session management, template/scale editors and nine-box/competency admin surfaces are deferred to a later phase (listed as 'available via API / coming to the console' rather than empty tabs). Keep use cases light.

useCases.title: HR reviews the performance cycle and team reviews
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test.
Open Performance.
Review the cycle list and completion stats; open a cycle's My Team Reviews / launch / release operations.
useCases.expected: The performance console renders the cycle list and review-operations surfaces. Deferred admin tabs (goals/OKR authoring, calibration sessions, scale/template editors) are signposted as coming/via-API rather than shown empty.

useCases.title: Employee views their own released review
steps: Log in as priya.nair@demo.test on the Employee portal.
Open Performance.
View own goals and, if a cycle rating has been released, the rating and acknowledge it.
useCases.expected: Priya sees only her own performance data. A final rating/manager comments are absent from the payload until the cycle is released; after release she can view and acknowledge.

useCases.title: Manager cannot open a non-report's review
steps: Log in as aarav.sharma@demo.test on the HR Admin portal.
Open Performance and view his team's reviews.
Attempt to open a review for an employee outside his reporting sub-tree (e.g. by altering the URL id).
useCases.expected: Only sub-tree reviews are listed; an out-of-team review id returns 404. A manager can never rate their own review (SoD).

features.title: Letters & Communication
features.summary: A first-class letters module: letterhead manager with a visual position-picker, versioned merge-field templates, an issue-a-letter wizard (preview -> reference number -> PDF), a tenant register with revoke/re-issue, and an ESS 'My Letters' surface.
features.howItWorks:
Configure once, issue per employee:
- HR uploads an A4 letterhead PDF and visually places the writing area + field anchors (date, ref no, authority, signature), then authors versioned merge-field templates (IN/NZ wording variants).
- Issue a letter: pick type -> pick a (scoped) employee -> fields auto-merge from the record -> editable live preview rendered onto the letterhead -> mint an atomic reference number -> flatten to PDF -> store as an employee-visible document -> audit. Contracts can route through built-in e-sign.
- A tenant register lists every issued letter (ref no/type/employee/status); revoke (reason, audited) and re-issue (new ref, supersede link) are supported.
- Compensation merge fields are masked unless the issuer can view comp.
Employees see and download their own letters with a tamper-integrity badge.
features.notes: Live (v1). Bulk/CSV issuance and a separate letter approval queue are deferred to v1.1.

useCases.title: Issue a letter to an employee via the wizard
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test.
Open Letters > Issue.
Pick a letter type/template, pick an employee, review the auto-merged live preview, then Issue now.
useCases.expected: A reference number is minted, a flattened PDF is rendered onto the letterhead and stored as an employee-visible document; the letter appears in the register and is downloadable.

useCases.title: Review the letter register and revoke a letter
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test and open Letters > Register.
Filter/search the register (ref no, type, employee, status).
On an issued letter, choose Revoke and provide a reason.
useCases.expected: The register lists issued letters with status. Revoke requires a reason, marks the letter Voided (audited, employee notified), and the reference number is burned (never reused).

useCases.title: Employee downloads their own letter with a tamper badge
steps: Log in as priya.nair@demo.test on the Employee portal.
Open Letters (My Letters).
Open/download one of her issued letters.
useCases.expected: Priya sees only her own issued (non-voided) letters with an integrity/tamper badge derived from the file hash; she can download the PDF. She cannot access another employee's letters.

features.title: Domain & Branding (Self-Service)
features.summary: White-label self-service: a tenant sets its branded subdomain, logo and brand color so employees see a branded Employee portal. Owner-gated.
features.howItWorks:
Subdomain + branding self-service:
- The tenant picks a subdomain slug; the system provisions {slug}-staging.drifthr.com (DNS + SSL) and binds it, so employees land on a branded portal.
- Slug changes are guarded: reserved slugs and collisions return a clear conflict, there is a change cooldown, and the new host goes live before the old one is removed.
- Branding: upload a logo, set a single brand HEX color, and see a 'what your employees see' preview.
- Custom domains (hr.acme.com via Cloudflare-for-SaaS) are built but gated behind a readiness flag; until enabled the section shows a 'coming soon' teaser.
Owner-gated: only canEditDomain/canEditBranding holders see the controls; Managers/Employees get 403/hidden.
features.notes: v1 = subdomain self-service + branding (live on staging). Custom-domain (Mode B) is feature-gated off until a one-time Cloudflare-for-SaaS enablement; the UI shows it as a teaser. Tester note: do NOT change the production demo slug unless instructed.

useCases.title: Owner reviews subdomain + branding settings
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test (Owner).
Open Settings > Domain.
Review the live subdomain address card (copy/open), the subdomain section, and the gated custom-domain 'coming soon' teaser.
useCases.expected: The address card shows the live subdomain with copy/open; the custom-domain section renders as a feature-gated teaser (not an error). Slug-change controls are present and Owner-gated.

useCases.title: Owner updates logo and brand color
steps: Log in as operator@demo.test and open Settings > Branding.
Upload/replace the logo and enter a brand HEX color.
Check the 'what your employees see' brand preview, then save.
useCases.expected: The logo uploads (or degrades gracefully to a URL field if storage is unconfigured), the HEX color validates, and the preview reflects the brand. Saves succeed for the Owner.

useCases.title: Non-owner cannot edit domain/branding
steps: Log in as aarav.sharma@demo.test on the HR Admin portal.
Attempt to reach Settings > Domain / Branding.
useCases.expected: The domain/branding settings are hidden from the nav for a non-owner; direct navigation is denied (403) — only Owner-level users may edit them.

features.title: Employee Self-Service (ESS)
features.summary: The white-label employee portal where an employee self-serves: dashboard/feed, profile, leave, attendance, payslips, documents, directory and tax — all strictly scoped to themselves.
features.howItWorks:
Self-service on the branded employee domain:
- The employee logs in at demo-staging.drifthr.com and lands on their dashboard/feed.
- Every read is self-derived from the session — there is no employeeId in any ESS path, so cross-employee access is structurally impossible.

features.title: Approval Workflows & Friendly RBAC
features.summary: A configurable approval engine plus a friendly RBAC/hierarchy surface: a non-technical admin draws an approval chain per process (manager -> finance, amount-tiered, parallel, SLA) and manages roles and the org tree — supporting both a 3-person and a 100-person tenant.
features.howItWorks:
One engine routes every approval; one friendly surface manages who-approves and who-reports-to-whom:
- Workflow builder: per process (Leave, Reimbursement, Travel, etc.) draw steps answering 'who says yes?' — my manager / N-up / a specific person / a role / auto-approve — in sequence or parallel, with 'only if amount > X' rules and SLA time-limits (remind/escalate/auto-decide). - RBAC: a Simple mode (five preset role cards) for small tenants, an Advanced mode (granular permission builder + scope band + time-bound grants) for big ones.

features.title: Reimbursement, Claims & Travel
features.summary: Claims and travel with a custom policy engine: employees claim expenses or apply for a trip, every bill is auto-validated against a per-diem/hotel/transport policy, and approvals run through the configured chain within the manager's scope.
features.howItWorks:
Claim -> auto-validate -> approve in scope -> settle:
- HR builds a Travel & Expense policy: per-diem caps by trip duration, a hotel budget matrix (employee level x city tier), and allowed transport modes with fare/eligibility rules; plus per-category limits and an enforcement mode (Flag vs Hard).
- Employee (ESS) files a standalone reimbursement (claim ID EXP-####) or applies for a trip (travel ID TRV-####) and submits bills against it; each bill gets a live policy verdict (within budget / over -> flagged / not allowed -> hard-blocked).

- Finance settles (payment ref) or pushes the net into payroll.
Policy rules are snapshotted at submit, so a later policy edit never changes a settled claim's verdict.

features.title: Income-Tax Regime Election (Old vs New)
features.summary: India employees elect their income-tax regime (Old vs New) for the financial year — seeing the live Old-vs-New tax comparison so the choice is informed — while HR sets the employer default, the election window, and a lock that freezes the year. Monthly TDS withholding follows the elected regime, falling back to the employer default for un-elected employees.
features.howItWorks:
Regime election sits on top of the regime-aware TDS engine and the IT projection:
- ESS (employee): on the Tax page a Regime card shows the OLD-vs-NEW projected annual tax (with a “Saves more” hint on the better regime) and the employee elects New or Old for the FY. The choice persists to /api/hr/me/tax/regime and immediately drives their monthly TDS. After HR locks (or the window closes) the card is read-only with the reason + date.
- Resolver: an employee who has NOT elected is withheld under the EMPLOYER DEFAULT (TaxRegimePolicy.defaultRegime), not a blanket New — getEffectiveRegime resolves elected → default → statutory New, and the payroll run consults it.
- HR (Tax → Tax regime): set the per-FY default regime, the election window (opens / locks dates), and a global lock; view every employee’s elected vs effective regime + lock status (paginated, searchable); lock a single employee or “lock all for FY” when the window closes.
- Enforcement: an election is rejected once the employee is locked, the window has closed, hasn’t opened, or the FY is globally locked. Every election appends a StatutoryElectionHistory audit row (old→new, effective from FY start).
features.notes: India-only. Withholding honours the effective regime (elected else employer default). Lock/window enforced server-side; ESS is SELF_ONLY (subject from the session). HR policy/lock writes gate on canManageStatutory; the per-employee view on canViewPayrollReports.

features.title: Salary Disbursement (India)
features.summary: Turn a frozen / approved pay run into a bank-uploadable salary-advice file (HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak, SBI or a generic NEFT/RTGS CSV), then reconcile the bank UTRs back onto each employee. India-only; money in integer paise end-to-end.
features.howItWorks:
A PayoutBatch is the unit of disbursement: one pay run rendered for one bank rail. It can only be created from a run whose totals are committed (Frozen/Approved/Paid/Filed) — Draft/Computed/In-review runs are refused.

- Create a batch: the service snapshots each PayRunLine net pay + the employee's primary active bank account into PayoutLines. Employees with no/invalid bank account (e.g. a missing IFSC) are FLAGGED and excluded — they never silently drop or crash the batch.
- Money round-trips: sum(PayoutLine.amountMinor) == PayoutBatch.totalMinor == the run net, all in integer paise (no floats).
- Generate the advice file: a PURE per-bank formatter (golden-tested, byte-pinned) renders the exact upload layout; this stamps the batch as generated (Queued -> Processing). Upload the file to your corporate net-banking.
- Reconcile: upload the bank's UTR / status export (CSV). Each line is matched by employee code or account number; status (Credited/Failed/Returned) + UTR update per employee and roll up the batch (Partial / Credited / Failed). Idempotent and re-runnable.
- An optional payout-gateway path (RazorpayX/Cashfree) is a pluggable seam; with no gateway configured the bank-file + reconcile path is the product. Account numbers appear only inside the file — the on-screen table masks them.
features.notes: Live. The six bank formatters are byte-pinned golden tests (the contract). The orchestrator (create -> file -> reconcile) is proven against the live test DB including tenant isolation (cross-tenant batch 404s), the no-over-pay guard (no 2nd batch once one is Credited), and the bank-detail offender-flagging. India-only — a non-IN run returns 422. create/file/reconcile are gated on canRunPayroll; reads on canViewPayrollReports.

After download the batch status shows Processing and a "generated" timestamp.

features.title: Public Signup, Email Verification & Disposable-Email Guard
features.summary: The front door: a prospect creates a DriftHR account, proves they own the email via a 6-digit OTP, and throwaway/disposable inboxes are refused. No usable account exists until the email is verified.
features.howItWorks:
Signup is atomic and verification-gated:

- The /api/auth/register endpoint validates the email with a Zod schema that rejects ~121k known disposable domains (yopmail.com, mailinator.com, 10minutemail.com, …) BEFORE anything is persisted.
- The 6-digit OTP email is sent via SES FIRST; only if the provider accepts the address is the user row written. A mail-provider rejection returns an error and creates no orphan account.
- register issues NO session cookie — the account is unusable until the OTP is verified at /api/auth/verify-otp, which then issues the session.
- Sender identity is no-reply@mail.drifthr.com (a DKIM-verified SES identity). In production the code reaches the real inbox; on staging all mail is rerouted to the QA override inbox.
features.notes: Disposable-email blocking is a static list lookup (no MX/DNS call), so it is deterministic and offline-safe. A genuine config gap (missing sender identity) now surfaces as a transient 'temporary problem' error rather than wrongly blaming the recipient's inbox.

useCases.title: Signup with a real email creates the account and sends a verification code

Enter a full name, a REAL (non-disposable) email address you can access, and a password meeting the rule (8+ chars, one uppercase, one lowercase, one number).
Tick the Terms of Service / Privacy Policy checkbox.
Click "Create account".
useCases.expected: The form is accepted and advances to the 6-digit code-entry screen with the message 'Account created. Check your email for the 6-digit verification code.' A verification email from no-reply@mail.drifthr.com arrives (on staging it lands in the QA override inbox). Entering the correct code verifies the account and signs you in; no session exists before verification.

features.title: ESS Shift Swap — request a swap
features.summary: An employee can request a shift swap from their My Shifts page: pick a colleague, choose the day they give and the day they take, add a reason, and send it. The colleague must consent before it goes to a manager.
features.howItWorks: On /shifts the employee sees a "Request a shift swap" form. The counterparty is chosen from the tenant-wide company directory (the SELF-scoped /api/hr/me/directory search), whose item id is the employee id sent as counterpartyEmployeeId. The form POSTs { counterpartyEmployeeId, requesterDate, counterpartyDate, reason } to POST /api/hr/me/shifts/swaps; the requester is resolved server-side from the session (never client-supplied). The "your day" picker is seeded from the published roster; the backend rejects unpublished/locked days and self-swaps. On success the swaps list refreshes and the new request shows as PENDING consent.
features.notes: Frontend-only change in apps/ess/app/shifts/page.js; reuses the existing createMySwap controller/route (no new endpoint) and the existing directory read for the counterparty picker.

useCases.title: An employee requests a shift swap with a colleague
steps: Open My Shifts.
Under Swap requests, click "Request a shift swap".
In "Swap with", search a colleague by name and select them.
Pick one of your published days under "Your day to give".
Pick the colleague’s day under "Their day to take" and enter a reason.
Click "Send swap request".
useCases.expected: The form submits, a success notice appears, and the new request shows in the swap list as Sent, with Consent = PENDING and Status = PENDING. No employeeId is sent for yourself — the requester is taken from your session.

useCases.title: You cannot swap a shift with yourself
steps: Open My Shifts and start a "Request a shift swap".
Attempt to select yourself as the counterparty (or submit with your own identity).
Submit the form.
useCases.expected: The backend rejects the request (400 "Cannot swap with yourself"); the form shows the error and no swap is created.
